text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
ROBERT BROWNING was born in 1812. The English poet's most successful poem was "The Last Duchess".
German composer JOHANNES BRAHMS was born in 1833. He was famous for his piano and violin concertos.
Russian composer PETER TCHAIKOVSKY was born in 1840. His most famous works were the ballets "Swan Lake" and "The Nutcracker".

Victorian railway administrator SIR HAROLD CLAPP was born in 1875. He was nicknamed CLEVER MARY after a popular household cleaner because he cleaned up the railways. His most lasting contribution to Australia was the invention of Raisin Toast.
JOSIP BROZ TITO, Yugoslav partisan leader and later president of post-war Yugoslavia from 1945 until 1980, was born in 1892.
American film star GARY COOPER was born in 1901. He won oscars for the films "Sergeant York" and "High Noon", and was also one of the first Hollywood heart throbs.
Singer JIMMY RUFFIN was born in 1939. The American soul artist's greatest hit was "What Becomes of the Broken-Hearted".

American singer/songwriter BILL DANOFF was born in 1946. He wrote "Take Me Home, Country Roads" with JOHN DENVER. He and his wife TAFFY formed Starland Vocal Band and had a hit with "Afternoon Delight" (1976).
** EVENTS **
1663 : In London, the first Theatre Royal in Drury Lane
was opened under a charter granted by King CHARLES II.
1765 : HMS Victory, the British battleship and flagship
of Lord NELSON, was launched at Chatham, Kent.
1832 : OTTO of Bavaria was chosen king of Greece by the
great powers at the conference of London.
1888 : American inventor GEORGE EASTMAN unveiled his box
camera which he claimed was the easiest in the world to use. He called the camera a KODAK, and set up the company of the same name to build the camera.
1911 : Thousands marched down New York's Fifth Avenue
demanding the vote for women.
1915 : The Cunard liner LUSITANIA was torpedoed by a
German U-Boat off the coast of 1200 passengers died. The sinking prompted the Americans to enter the First World War.
1926 : The voting age for British women was lowered from
1942 : Japanese, American, and Australian Naval Forces
clashed in the Battle of the Coral Sea.
1945 : Germany formally surrendered to the Allies during
World War Two.
1954 : In North Vietnam, the Vietminh siege of French
forces at Dien Bien Phu ended with the surrender of the French.
1977 : Ninety thousand tickets for BOB DYLAN's London
concert sold out in eight hours.
1979 : In Brisbane, LINDA JONES became the first woman
jockey to ride a winner against men in Australia. She was riding "Pay The Purple".
1979 : In Teheran, Ayatollah KHOMEINI lowered the age of
marriage for girls to 13 and for boys to 15.
1988 : Boston hosted the first gathering of people who
claimed to have been abducted by aliens.
1994 : The stolen masterpiece "The Scream" by EDVARD
MUNCH was found undamaged in a hotel in south Norway.
1995 : JACQUES CHIRAC won the French presidential
election, beating Socialist opponent LIONEL JOSPIN by a clear margin and ending a 14-year Socialist grip on the presidency.
